newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes little changed, feedgrains lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes little changed, feedgrains lower.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed little changed, with crusher-related buying offset by late scale-up commercial selling, floor sources said.

Dealers said weakness in new crop CBOT soybeans weighed on new crop canola prices, although continued talk that Canadian canola plantings may be lower than originally expected helped to cushion losses.

Statistics Canada is due to issue its first plantings report Wednesday, based on intentions at the end of March, and some believe the report may overstate canola area as recent strength in wheat prices is expected to cut into oilseed acreage.
July canola closed off $0.40 at $430.40, with new crop November $1.30 lower at $380.50.
Flaxseed was lower in very quiet trade, with July off $1.30 at $342.70.
Western barley ended lower with commercial liquidating of May longs ahead of Wednesday's first notice day. July closed down $1.00 at $139.90. Weaker CBOT corn weighed on the market.
Wheat was also lower with both commission houses and commercials liquidating May longs. July closed down $2.60 at $169.90. May feed peas ended unchanged at US$217.00. Oats remained tradeless.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
